claim: Albright remembered a little Serbian from her days in Belgrade as a child.

evidence.quote: As you can see, I remember a little Serbian -- albeit with a Czech accent -- from my days in Belgrade as a child.
Secretary of State Madeleine K. Albright Remarks to the Serbian People March 26, 1999, Washington, D.C

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Belgrade stop. Albright's own words in remarks released by the Office of the Spokesman.

claim: Albright's father was a Czechoslovak diplomat in Belgrade before the Second World War.

evidence.quote: from my days in Belgrade as a child. My father was a Czechoslovak diplomat there before the Second World War.
Secretary of State Madeleine K. Albright Remarks to the Serbian People March 26, 1999, Washington, D.C

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Belgrade stop.

claim: When the Nazis invaded Czechoslovakia, Albright's father escaped to Yugoslavia with his wife and baby.

evidence.quote: When the Nazis invaded Czechoslovakia, my father escaped to Yugoslavia with his wife and baby -- me.
Secretary of State Madeleine K. Albright Remarks to the Serbian People March 26, 1999, Washington, D.C

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Belgrade stop; the travel leg from Prague. The source names Yugoslavia, not a city, for the escape.

claim: Albright's father, Josef, was press attaché in Belgrade, Yugoslavia.

evidence.quote: Her father, Josef, was a member of the Czechoslovak Foreign Service and served as press attaché in Belgrade, Yugoslavia

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Belgrade stop (atomic part of the Office of the Historian biography sentence).

claim: Albright's father, Josef, later became Ambassador to Yugoslavia.

evidence.quote: Her father, Josef, was a member of the Czechoslovak Foreign Service and served as press attaché in Belgrade, Yugoslavia and later became Ambassador to Yugoslavia.

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Belgrade stop (postwar posting).

claim: Albright's father had served as the Ambassador from Czechoslovakia to Yugoslavia shortly after World War II.

evidence.quote: Albright’s father had served as the Ambassador from Czechoslovakia to Yugoslavia shortly after World War II.

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Belgrade stop; dates the ambassadorship. Same holder (U.S. Department of State) as ALB-S-0012.

claim: Albright was hiding in shelters as German bombs fell on London.

evidence.quote: having experienced the horrors of war firsthand – fleeing Czechoslovakia after the Nazis invaded, then hiding in shelters as German bombs fell on London

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: London stop. No institutional source found that names a London address; see TOUR-RESEARCH.md gaps.

claim: Albright steamed into New York Harbor, past the Statue of Liberty.

evidence.quote: So, like countless others before and since, we steamed into New York Harbor, past the Statue of Liberty, with tears in our eyes and hope in our hearts.

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: arrival stop. Albright's own words at the 1998 naturalization ceremony; the date of arrival is in ALB-F-0082 and ALB-F-0064.

claim: Albright arrived in the United States with her mother, her sister and her brother.

evidence.quote: 50 years ago tomorrow, I arrived here in the United States for the first time. With me was my mother, my sister and my brother

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: arrival stop.

claim: Albright arrived in the United States as a young girl aboard the SS America in 1948.

evidence.quote: When she arrived in the United States as a young girl aboard the SS America in 1948, she never dreamt that she would become our nation’s first female Secretary of State.

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: arrival stop, travel leg (ship name). Only source found for the ship name; secondary (bushcenter.org is not in the registry). Not corroborated by a passenger manifest (see TOUR-RESEARCH.md).

claim: The Rockefeller Foundation found Albright's father a job at the University of Denver in Colorado.

evidence.quote: The Rockefeller Foundation found her father a job at the University of Denver in Colorado
evidence.locator: article, paragraph on the family's arrival

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Denver stop. Atomic restatement of the first half of ALB-F-0018, which the adversary found not atomic; ALB-F-0018 is left for the reviewer.

claim: Albright graduated from Kent Denver School.

evidence.quote: Albright spent her teen years in Denver and graduated from Kent Denver School

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Denver stop. ALB-S-0115 (Rocky Mountain PBS) repeats this 'according to her biography in the Colorado Women's Hall of Fame', so it is not independent and is not cited.

claim: Albright received a B.A. with honors from Wellesley College.

evidence.quote: Dr. Albright received a B.A. with Honors from Wellesley College
She received a B.A. with honors from Wellesley College

notes: Tour research albright-tour-2026-10-15: Wellesley stop.
